subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines resource security?
options: Having reliable and affordable access to a sufficient quantity of a resource
Owning all of a country's natural resources privately
Exporting more resources than a country imports
Storing resources only for use during wartime
questions.explain: Resource security means a reliable, affordable and sufficient supply of a resource to meet a population's needs.

questions.q: Food security exists when people have:
options: Physical and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food
Access to fast food outlets in their local area
Enough farmland to grow crops only for export
A diet based only on locally grown produce
questions.explain: Food security is reliable physical and economic access to enough safe, nutritious food to stay healthy and active.

questions.q: Water security means having reliable access to:
options: Unlimited free water for industry only
questions.explain: Water security is dependable access to enough clean, affordable water for drinking, sanitation and economic activity.

questions.q: A country has energy security when it has:
options: A reliable and affordable supply of energy
No need to import any fuel ever
The lowest energy prices in the world
questions.explain: Energy security is an uninterrupted, affordable supply of energy to meet a country's needs.

questions.q: Which group of resources is finite (non-renewable)?
questions.explain: Fossil fuels such as coal, oil and natural gas are finite and cannot be replaced within a human timescale.

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy source?
questions.explain: Solar power is renewable because sunlight is naturally replenished and does not run out.

questions.q: Which strategy helps reduce the amount of resources sent to landfill?
options: Burning all household waste in the open
questions.explain: Reducing, reusing and recycling conserves raw materials and cuts the volume of waste sent to landfill.

questions.q: Which combination best explains rising global demand for resources?
questions.explain: More people and rising wealth increase consumption of food, water and energy, driving up demand.

questions.q: Why does energy demand tend to rise as a country develops economically?
options: Industrialisation and greater use of technology and appliances
People use less electricity as incomes rise
questions.explain: Economic development brings industry, transport and more household appliances, all of which raise energy demand.

options: Demand for water exceeds the amount physically available in an area
People cannot afford the infrastructure to access water
Water is available but only slightly polluted
A country simply chooses not to import water
questions.explain: Physical water scarcity happens where there is not enough water in the environment to meet demand.

questions.q: Economic water scarcity is best described as:
options: Water is available but people lack the money or infrastructure to access it
There is physically not enough water in the region
Water is too cold to be used
All water is reserved for shipping
questions.explain: Economic water scarcity means water exists but poverty or a lack of infrastructure prevents access to it.

options: The water used to produce goods and food that are then traded
Water stored deep underground in aquifers
Water vapour held in the atmosphere
questions.explain: Virtual water is the hidden water used to grow or manufacture traded goods, effectively transferring water between places.

questions.q: Which factor can limit a country's supply of a resource such as water?
options: The colour of the national flag
questions.explain: Physical factors such as climate, geology and relief strongly influence how much of a resource is available.

questions.q: Sustainable resource use means using resources in a way that:
options: Meets present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs
Uses up resources as quickly as possible
questions.explain: Sustainability balances current needs with conserving resources and the environment for the future.

questions.q: One reason renewable energy supports sustainability is that it:
options: Does not run out and produces lower carbon emissions than fossil fuels
Is always cheaper than every other energy source
Produces more greenhouse gases than coal
questions.explain: Renewables are replenished naturally and emit far less carbon than fossil fuels, supporting long-term sustainability.

questions.q: A country suffers repeated droughts that reduce harvests and force it to import more food. This is an example of increasing:
questions.explain: Falling home production and greater reliance on imports reduce reliable access to food, increasing food insecurity.

questions.q: A rapidly industrialising country's factories and growing middle class use far more electricity each year. This best illustrates:
questions.explain: Industrial growth and rising affluence push up electricity consumption, increasing demand for energy resources.

questions.q: A city introduces water metering, fixes leaking pipes and promotes low-flush toilets. These strategies mainly aim to:
options: Manage demand and use water more sustainably
questions.explain: Metering, leak repair and efficient fittings cut waste and manage demand, using water more sustainably.

questions.q: A government offers subsidies for household solar panels and wind farms to cut reliance on imported gas. This strategy is designed to improve:
questions.explain: Boosting domestic renewables reduces import reliance and emissions, improving both energy security and sustainability.
